'''''Rubus ulmifolius''''' is a species of [[blackberry]] native to western and southern Europe and northwestern Africa. It has also become widely [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] elsewhere in Europe, and in northern India, the Americas, southern Africa, and Australasia.<ref name="POWO">{{cite web |title=Plants of the World Online |website=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:740982-1 |access-date=2026-08-07}}</ref>

==Description==
''Rubus ulmifolius'' is a bramble [[shrub]] that typically grows to {{convert|2|–|3|m}} tall, adapted to more open, sunny habitats than many other blackberries. It usually has numerous small [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|prickles]]. The [[leaves]] are palmately compound with 3 or 5 leaflets, the leaflets green on the upper surface but greenish-white on the underside because of a dense layer of woolly hairs.<ref name="Brambles">{{cite web |title=Brambles of the British Isles - Rubus ulmifolius |website=www.jnecology.uk |url=https://www.jnecology.uk/rubus/accounts/ulmifolius.htm |access-date=2026-08-07}}</ref><ref name="Mehiou">{{cite journal |last1=Mehiou |first1=Afaf |last2=Alla |first2=Chaimae |last3=Akissi |first3=Zachee L. E. |last4=Lucau-Danila |first4=Anca |last5=Bouanani |first5=Nourelhouda |last6=Legssyer |first6=Abdelkhaleq |last7=Hilbert |first7=Jean-Louis |last8=Sahpaz |first8=Sevser |last9=Ziyyat |first9=Abderrahim |title=''Rubus ulmifolius'' Schott: A comprehensive review of its botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry and pharmacological effects |journal=Journal of Berry Research |volume=14 |issue=4 |date=2024 |issn=1878-5093 |doi=10.1177/18785093241283261 |pages=301–328 |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/18785093241283261 |access-date=2026-08-07|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The flowers are usually pink, sometimes white. The fruit is a compound drupe, ripening dark purple to almost black.<ref name="Brambles"/>

''Rubus ulmifolius'' is unique among subgenus ''Rubus'' in displaying normal sexual reproduction; all other species are facultative [[apomicts]].<ref name="Brambles"/><ref name="Edees, E.S. 1988">Edees, E.S., Newton, A. and Kent, D.H., 1988. Brambles of the British Isles. Ray Society.</ref>

{{gallery|mode=packed

A spineless form, ''Rubus ulmifolius'' [[form (botany)|f.]] ''inermis'' (Wild.) Rehd., is the progenitor of a number of [[cultivar]]s grown for fruit, which is more easily harvested than in natural spiny forms.<ref name="TSO">{{cite web |title=Rubus ulmifolius |website=Trees and Shrubs Online |date=2026-08-06 |url=https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/rubus/rubus-ulmifolius/ |access-date=2026-08-07}}</ref>

== Subspecies ==
[[Rubus ulmifolius subsp. sanctus|''Rubus sanctus'']] is often considered to be a subspecies of ''R. ulmifolius''.{{cn|date=August 2026}}

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Rubus ulmifolius'' is found in its native range across Western Europe, from the [[Netherlands]] south to [[Spain]] and [[Portugal]], in [[Great Britain|Britain]] and [[Ireland]], as well as northwest [[Africa]].
